title: confed comment result
description: The `result` of `confed comment <subcommand> --json`; each subcommand has its own shape. `list` reads the local copy of a page's comments, or the server's for a page id the workspace does not track. `add`, `reply` and `resolve` write drafts that the next push posts, or post them now with --push. `edit` and `rm` act on the server at once; `prune-markers` takes orphan inline-comment markers out of a page.

list.description: `list`: the comments of a page in the workspace, from the local copy.

source.description: Read from the workspace's copy; `server` in the other shape.

orphan_markers.description: Inline-comment markers in the page that belong to no comment.

checked_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the last time comments were read from the server, or null if never.

refreshed.description: --refresh read them from the server just now.

changed.description: With --refresh only: the server's comments differed from the local copy.

list_live.description: `list` of a page id the workspace does not track: read from the server, with a warning saying so.

created.description: When it was posted, as the server gives it.

resolved.description: Its thread is resolved: a reply has no status of its own, and is as resolved as its thread.

thread_resolved.description: The same as `resolved`, by design: named for what it says of a reply.

reply_to.description: The comment it replies to; null for a thread's root.

anchor.description: An inline thread root's anchor; null for page comments and replies.

text.description: The page text the comment is on.

orphaned.description: That text can no longer be found in the page.

placed.description: Local list only: a mark for it is in the page file.

line.description: Local list only: the line of that mark in the page file.

text.description: The page text the marker wraps.

add.description: `add`: a draft written to the page body (an inline comment the body can carry a mark for) or to the comments.md sidecar; with --push, posted.

draft.description: Still a draft: no --push, or the push failed.

body.description: The comment as given, in Markdown.

anchor.description: --anchor: the text an inline comment is on; null for a page comment.

written_to.description: `body`: a `<!--c new …-->` mark in the page file. `sidecar`: an entry in comments.md.

line.description: `body` only: the line of the mark in the page file.

sidecar_reason.description: `sidecar` only: why an inline comment could not go into the page body; null when it did not have to.

posted.description: --push: the ids of the comments posted.

comments.description: --push: what was posted, as the server reported it.

marker_ref.description: An inline comment's marker ref in the page.

push_counts.description: --push: the comment work the push did, as ids.

reply.description: `reply`: the same reply queued on each thread named; with --push, posted.

draft.description: Still a draft: no --push, or the push failed.

result.description: The same as `push`, under its old name; read `push`.

posted.description: --push: the ids of the replies posted.

replies.description: --push: each reply posted, under the parent the server keeps. An inline thread is one level deep, so a reply to a reply sits under the thread's root.

reply_to.description: The comment it was asked to reply to.

parent.description: The comment it was posted under.

resolve.description: `resolve`: resolves queued in the sidecar for the threads named, or every open thread of a page (--all); with --push, applied.

draft.description: Resolves wait in the sidecar: some were queued and no --push was given, or the push failed.

result.description: The same as `push`, under its old name; read `push`.

edit.description: `edit`: a posted comment changed on the server.

rm.description: `rm`: posted comments deleted on the server, with their replies. Declining the prompt returns {"deleted": [], "cancelled": true}.

prune_markers.description: `prune-markers`: the orphan inline-comment markers taken out of the page, or with --dry-run that would be.
